entries.reason: a capture scope over a Metal 4 queue, which is the scope the port already makes over a Metal 3 one - a device and a queue, recorded and starting nothing
entries.effect: the value the application set, read back, with Apple's own answer measured on a host and written down in tests/backports/device/metalchain-expectations.h; the port's queue is an EAGL object over OpenGL ES 2.0 and cannot be built in a host binary, so the CHECK against those expectations is HELD BY THE DEVICE PROBE, WHICH HAS NOW RUN, THREE TIMES on the emulated iPhone3,1 6.1.3 10B329 on 2026-10-04: "metalchain: 18 check(s), 2 failure(s), 12 not answered" with all fourteen queue members answering on CharonMetalDevice, "18 check(s), 0 failure(s), 14 not answered" with them on the queue, and "18 check(s), 2 failure(s), 12 not answered" again now that the two commits are `owed` rather than defined, because they need a buffer this port does not carry. NO case behind the device was exercised in any of the three: the guest makes no EAGL context. This row's own case is named in the run: "ok MTLCaptureScope_over_a_Metal4_queue: -[MTLCaptureManager newCaptureScopeWithMTL4CommandQueue:] answers a scope over the port's queue" - the probe asks the scope factory itself, over the port's own CharonMetal4CommandQueue, and it needs no device: the manager is the release's own and a scope is a device and a queue, recorded. What is NOT verified on that guest, and why, is measured in the run's own lines: "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 2.0 on this guest: NIL" and "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 1.1 on this guest: NIL", with the run's emulator.log naming the renderer "Shade GLES 1.1 Vulkan (SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0))", so MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice answers nil there and every case that needs the port's device has no object to ask. entries.reason: the commit is the queue's only submit call and this port cannot do it yet: both forms take an array of MTL4CommandBuffer and the port carries no MTL4CommandBuffer - the buffer is the next family, and every buffer a Metal 4 caller could hand the commit would be one this port did not make. A method that answers wrongly is worse than one that is absent, so this row is `owed` rather than `implemented` and NO method is defined for it: check_registry holds a row that is not implemented to an answer the build does not give
entries.effect: THE METHOD IS NOT DEFINED ON ANY CLASS, and that is the state of the row: `nm` on the probe binary of 2026-10-04 (tests/backports/device/metalchain-probe/run) carries -[CharonMetal4CommandQueue commit:count:] and, before the fix, the same selector only on -[CharonMetalDevice(CharonMetal4CommandQueue26) commit:count:] - the fourteen members of this protocol were answering on the device and on no queue, which is what the corpus recorded as `missing` for all of them (coordination/corpus/ledger-2026-10-03/Metal.tsv). The device probe's run of 2026-10-04 on the emulated iPhone3,1 6.1.3 10B329 could NOT ask it: "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 2.0 on this guest: NIL" and "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 1.1 on this guest: NIL", with the run's emulator.log naming the renderer "Shade GLES 1.1 Vulkan (SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0))", so MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice answers nil there (Metal/CharonMetalDevice.m:30-38) and every case behind the device has no object to ask. The case this waits on is metalchain_commit_returns (and metalchain_commit_returns_when_not_ended), which the same run reports as "FAIL metalchain_commit_returns: the queue answers -commit:count: (Apple's own queue does)" - the queue does not answer it, because the row is owed and not because the placement is wrong. It comes back with Metal/MTL4CommandBuffer26.m.

entries.effect: the call returns and a line in the device's log names the facility it would have needed, which is how this port refuses a void method (Metal/MTLComputeCommandEncoder8.m:145); CHECKED ON THE GUEST by the device probe's own line, on the emulated iPhone3,1 6.1.3 10B329 of 2026-10-04: "ok   MTL4CommandQueue_refusal: the port's -[MTL4CommandQueue copyBufferMappingsFromBuffer:toBuffer:operations:count:] returns and does not raise", with the refusal itself in the same log as a "Metal: " line naming the facility - the port refuses a void method with NSLog (Metal/MTLComputeCommandEncoder8.m:145) and the guest's output carries it; run-guest.sh counts those lines against the refusals the probe reported and the run of 2026-10-04 gave "12 refusal(s) reported, 12 refusal line(s) in the guest output". What is checked is the return and the presence of the refusal, which is what a caller can see`nm` on the probe binary of 2026-10-04 (tests/backports/device/metalchain-probe/run) carries -[CharonMetal4CommandQueue copyBufferMappingsFromBuffer:toBuffer:operations:count:] and, before the fix, the same selector only on -[CharonMetalDevice(CharonMetal4CommandQueue26) copyBufferMappingsFromBuffer:toBuffer:operations:count:] - the fourteen members of this protocol were answering on the device and on no queue, which is what the corpus recorded as `missing` for all of them (coordination/corpus/ledger-2026-10-03/Metal.tsv).  The device probe's run of 2026-10-04 on the emulated iPhone3,1 6.1.3 10B329 could NOT ask it: "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 2.0 on this guest: NIL" and "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 1.1 on this guest: NIL", with the run's emulator.log naming the renderer "Shade GLES 1.1 Vulkan (SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0))", so MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice answers nil there (Metal/CharonMetalDevice.m:30-38) and every case behind the device has no object to ask.
